name: Driftwall Foam-Packed Insulated Boot — Steel Shank
description: A Shelf-grade winter boot built from reclaimed rubber outsoles, closed-cell foam inserts packed into salvaged leather-analog uppers, and sheet-metal ankle shanks for structural support. They're ugly, mismatched at the ankle seams, and rated for standing in slush for 12-hour shifts. Warm enough that Shelf residents trade them like currency mid-winter.
functionality: Waterproof to ankle depth in standing slush; insulated for static cold down to -25C; steel shank prevents outsole collapse on debris-strewn terrain.
what_it_says: Someone who knows exactly what happens to feet in a Shelf winter and refused to let it happen to theirs.
story_hooks: The right boot's foam insert has a data chip embedded in it — someone's insurance policy, or someone's dead drop.
These boots were traded for three days of generator access; the person who gave them up was gambling on a mild winter and lost.
